answer: Utility bills stop sybil farms. A newcomer shows a recent bill in their name at a real address, and the ledger checks it against the utility's public record; two auditors confirm the match in fourteen days, and a reused bill is rejected while a forged one bans it. One honest agent shows one bill; a thousand fakes need a thousand utility accounts at thirty dollars each, so the farm pays thirty thousand, while a summit stamp, a quartz meter, and a pigment seal mark every real bill.
